clue.text: Like some old furniture in a lump covered by fabric

indicators.note: a thing covered by something else sits inside it, so the fabric goes round the lump

parts.note: jean is a strong twilled cotton fabric
a cob is a lump or rounded piece, as of coal

explanation.surface: Describing antique furniture with a lumpy bit hidden under its upholstery.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture from the reign of James I is described by this period adjective, much like Tudor or Georgian pieces.

clue.text: Cheerful knave introducing female relation

indicators.note: the first piece introduces, coming before, the second

parts.note: J is the jack or knave in cards
an aunty is a female relative

explanation.surface: A cheery rogue bringing in his aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunty manner is lively and self-confident, much like cheerful.

clue.text: Suppression needed when steamy comedian comes out with spoonerism?

indicators.note: the clue asks us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as Dr Spooner did

parts.note: steamy means damp
a clown is a comedian

explanation.surface: A crackdown needed when a racy comic gets his words muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steamy comedian' gives DAMP CLOWN; swapping their opening sounds produces the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a firm suppression of something, such as dissent.

clue.text: Sharp female starts to be extremely critical, kicking you

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A tart woman begins to be harshly critical and kicks you.
explanation.walkthrough: Becky Sharp is the scheming heroine of Thackeray's Vanity Fair, so 'Sharp' is her surname, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adventuress of Vanity Fair is Rebecca Sharp, known by her pet name.

clue.text: Fuss over soft man chosen as candidate

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: Commotion about a gentle man selected to stand for election.
explanation.definitionFit: A party adopts a person when it selects them to stand for it.

clue.text: Injured when train goes into sea

indicators.note: one piece going into another is placed inside it

parts.note: the Med is the usual short name for the Mediterranean Sea
to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: A grim report of someone hurt when a railway train plunged into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway train but is the verb, as in training a weapon on a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone maimed has been badly wounded or disabled, so the past participle matches 'injured'.

clue.text: Salt in a nut meal I cooked

indicators.note: cooked means prepared and altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seasoning in a dish of nuts that I made.
explanation.definitionFit: An aluminate is a chemical salt containing aluminium and oxygen.

clue.text: Love lying in grass endlessly, having joined Stonehenge's foremost festival

indicators.note: one thing lying in another rests inside it
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: marram is a coarse ... of sand dunes
to dig something is to love it, in slang

indicators.note: foremost picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lover stretched out in the grass, then off to the Stonehenge solstice celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' as a verb is slang for liking something; 'lying in' puts it inside the shortened dune grass, and 'having joined' simply tacks on the initial of Stonehenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shrove Tuesday carnival, famous in New Orleans, is a festival.

clue.text: A daughter, outwardly respectable, may be anything but

definitions.text: A daughter, outwardly respectable, may be anything but

indicators.note: outwardly means the word is placed on the outside, round the rest

parts.note: decent means respectable

explanation.surface: A girl who looks respectable but may be anything of the sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' puts DECENT around A and D; read whole, the clue says she seems decent but is far from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-indulgent and morally degenerate is the opposite of respectable.

clue.text: Stop lying in bed

parts.note: a ship at anchor lies with its anchor in the sea bed; the order to raise it ends that rest, not a lazy morning

explanation.surface: An instruction to get up rather than lounge under the covers.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailing command means raise the anchor and set off, ending a vessel's stay at its mooring.

clue.text: Rules of game set by reliable person mostly

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for rugby union

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a brick is a dependable, good-hearted person

explanation.surface: A game's regulations drawn up by someone fairly trustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a set of directions or instructions, as printed at the head of an exam paper.

clue.text: Butler coming with starter of cold crustacean

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Rab Butler was a British Conservative politician of the mid-20th century

explanation.surface: A manservant arriving with a cold seafood starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler' looks like a servant but is R. A. 'Rab' Butler, a senior British Conservative minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab is a ten-legged shellfish, one of the crustaceans.

clue.text: Grower wants leaves, stems and shoots, say — but just the outer bits

parts.note: the top of a root crop is its leafy upper growth, as in carrot tops

indicators.note: only the first and last letters of the word say are kept here

explanation.surface: A gardener's demand for foliage and shoots, with a curious restriction to their edges.
explanation.walkthrough: Topsy, the child in Uncle Tom's Cabin, says she was never born but 'just growed', so she is the famous grower.
explanation.definitionFit: The slave girl in Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel claims she simply grew up unaided, giving the phrase 'grew like Topsy'.

clue.text: Tried playing with fire-making others this?

definitions.text: Tried playing with fire-making others this?

indicators.note: playing with letters means toying with them and rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone who has been playing with fire, with the result of frightening others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing with' rearranges TRIED and FIRE together; read whole, the clue says that playing with fire makes onlookers scared stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Those watching someone play with fire would be badly frightened, which is the condition the clue describes.

clue.text: Wicked chap for accumulating runs — going after famous duck

definitions.text: Wicked chap for accumulating runs — going after famous duck

indicators.note: the second part follows the first, coming after the cartoon duck

parts.note: the Disney cartoon duck

indicators.note: accumulating means gathering something in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a bad man is a wicked fellow
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A villain who scores heavily, following on from a celebrated nought.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, and the great Australian batsman famously made one in his last Test innings. The setter of this puzzle uses his surname as a pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian cricketer was the greatest accumulator of Test runs, averaging 99.94.

clue.text: One given envelope possibly dreads being given notice

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word could be arranged another way

parts.note: to see is to notice

explanation.surface: Someone handed an envelope may dread being served notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a letter is sent to receives the envelope bearing their name.

clue.text: See 14
Waver, that most desirable thing being completely unrealistic?

definitions.text: that most desirable thing being completely unrealistic?
definitions.meaning: an instant fix for every problem, too good to be true

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating over a dream that is wholly fanciful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waver' reads as hesitate but means something that is waved, as a conjuror's stick is.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror's stick is waved to perform wonders, and figuratively it is a fanciful quick solution.

clue.text: Those people's drink being consumed-a feature at Aintree

indicators.note: a drink being consumed is taken in, so it goes inside

parts.note: their means belonging to those people
cha is tea, a drink

explanation.surface: Racegoers having their drink at the Grand National course.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse of the Grand National, and The Chair is one of its biggest fences.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse's tallest steeplechase obstacle has this name, so it is a notable fixture there.

clue.text: Furtive advice after bad name has been given?

definitions.text: advice after bad name has been given?
definitions.meaning: the proverb 'give a dog a bad name and hang him', read as instructions

explanation.surface: Someone sneaking off after being told what to do once their reputation is ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepish, shamefaced look is furtive; the proverb about a dog with a bad name ends in hanging it.

clue.text: See 7
Assurance given in place by border

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A guarantee given somewhere close to a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise, a guarantee given to someone.

clue.text: Agent's got into shave in train

indicators.note: something that has got into another sits inside it

parts.note: to pare is to shave off a thin layer
a rep is a sales agent; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A sales agent has got into shaving on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare someone is to coach them for a task, as to train.

clue.text: Swift passage? Caution and hesitation required

parts.note: care is caution
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Moving fast requires care and a little hesitancy.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush headlong, so the noun use suggests a rapid course.

clue.text: Worker over a barrel had to work willingly with others

parts.note: a cooper is a craftsman who makes barrels
to have a meal is to eat it, so had is ate

explanation.surface: A labourer in a tight spot was forced to collaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over a barrel' suggests being helpless, but here it is literal: the man who builds barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: To collaborate is to act jointly and helpfully alongside other people.

clue.text: Where chalk may be put at the right moment

definitions.meaning: snooker players chalk the tip of their stick

explanation.surface: Where a snooker player puts chalk, done just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalk goes on a snooker stick; arriving promptly is arriving just as a prompt is given.

clue.text: Pronouncements in article at back of little word book

indicators.note: the article is placed behind, coming last

parts.note: dict is a short form of dictionary, a book of words
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Statements tucked into an article at the back of a small dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicta are authoritative statements or sayings, especially a judge's remarks.

clue.text: Girl clutching fashionable loincloth

indicators.note: one piece clutching another holds it inside

parts.note: Di is a girl's name
hot means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A girl holding on to a trendy garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The dhoti is a long cloth wrapped round the waist, worn by Hindu men.

clue.text: Entry showing tax on account

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a cess is a local tax or levy

explanation.surface: A ledger entry recording a tax charged to an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Access is a way in or the right to enter, much like an entrance.

clue.text: Restriction on extent of life peers

parts.note: a bar is a restriction or ban
age is the length of time someone has lived

explanation.surface: A limit on how long members of the House of Lords may serve.
explanation.definitionFit: The barons collectively, the nobility, are a body of noblemen of rank.

clue.text: Cannabis supplied by sailor?

definitions.meaning: a sailor who reefs, or shortens, sails could be called one who reefs

explanation.surface: Drugs being handed out by a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled marijuana cigarette has this slang name, and a sailor reefing sails would be a reefer.

clue.text: Nudge about to be given to bodyguard

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a minder is a bodyguard

explanation.surface: A gentle push concerning the security man.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt that jogs someone's memory is a nudge.
